text:
incident-bot: ALERT: streaming.p99 latency > 4s in us-west1 for /v1/stream (detected by realtime-latency-rule). p95=800ms p99=4.6s error-rate +3% :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: paging oncall — I'm on it. pulling dashboards now.

Maya: I see a sharp tail at ~13:12 UTC on the streaming tail-latency dashboard. spike corresponds to a rise in queue_length on runtime-hosts-usw-*.

Ash: any deploys recently? model rolling update earlier today at 11:40 UTC for tokenizer/kv-cache tweak.

Leo: I can confirm a canary rolled at 11:40 and then ramped to 50% at 12:05. I’m checking rollout notes.

oncall-sre: quick triage checklist: 1) impacted endpoints 2) region 3) rolling deploys 4) infra saturation 5) customer impact.

Maya: Impacted: streaming (long-lived SSE/chunking) and a few high-context generate calls. Region: us-west1 primarily. I’m seeing repeated Get/Put on KV cache and a lot of cache-miss churn.

Jordan: Support: two customers reported intermittent stalls and reconnects since ~12:10 UTC. No large-scale 5xx spike but many client aborts.

oncall-sre: Numbers: p95=800ms p99=4.6s, request rate steady. error-rate +3% (client aborts). Affected requests ~ 6k in last 10m.

Maya: Logs from runtime show streaming worker threads stuck in dequeue for 200-1000ms intermittently. Snip: ```runtime: stalled fetching kv chunk, key=ctx-abc123, attempt=3, backoff=120ms```

Ash: That matches a regression i saw in the kv eviction change — it increases lock contention under large concurrent prefix caching. If locks are contended, per-token stalls happen and streaming stalls amplify tail latency.

Leo: Current plan options: 1) rollback canary, 2) route streaming traffic to stable region (us-east1), 3) enable degraded-mode (disable streaming, fallback to chunked/generation polling), 4) scale up replicas to reduce per-host concurrency. Thoughts?

Sam: Product: customer impact is real — recommend quick mitigation that minimizes risk: route traffic and scale. Rolling back a runtime change could be ok but takes longer to validate.

oncall-sre: I'm going to push a temporary routing rule to divert 30% of new connections to us-east1 and scale the us-west runtime pool +20% now. Executing kubectl and routing change.

deploy-bot: runbook: apply traffic-split to edge-router: {us-west1:70, us-east1:30} — started.

oncall-sre: kubectl scale deployment runtime-usw --replicas=24 (was 20) — scaling initiated.

Maya: I'm going to throttle the new kv-cache lock path on canary hosts to force fallback to the old path. If that reduces contention we can confirm. Patch command: ```curl -X POST https://runtime-usw-canary/config -d '{"kv_lock_throttle":true}'```

Ash: Meanwhile I propose we pause the canary promotion. Leo, can you stop the ramp?

Leo: ramp paused and canary traffic frozen at current -> no further promotion.

Maya: After throttling canary, p99 dropped from 4.6s -> 2.1s in ~60s. queue_length on canaries reduced.

oncall-sre: Good signal. Continue: keep routing split and scale up until p99 < 1.0s or stable for 10m.

Jordan: Noting customer comms: sending interim update to affected customers: "We detected latency spikes for streaming in us-west1; mitigation underway and we routed traffic to alternate region. We'll follow up with RCA."

Ash: Root cause hypothesis: kv cache lock behavior change under heavy concurrent streaming caused head-of-line stalls; compounding effect for long-lived streaming sessions.

Maya: Short-term mitigations summary (completed/in progress):
- throttle canary kv lock path (in-progress)
- pause canary ramp (done)
- increase runtime replicas (in-progress)
- split traffic to us-east1 (done)
- disable client-side long context for new sessions (optional)

oncall-sre: Metrics after actions: p95=420ms p99=880ms (after 6m). error-rate back to baseline. continuing to monitor.

Sam: Can we put a temporary rule to drop streaming session keepalive > 45s for new sessions to lower concurrency? Product prefers we avoid breaking customer experience unless necessary.

Maya: We can add a gating policy for new sessions: max_context_tokens=1024 for new streaming sessions — that is lower risk than cutting streaming entirely. Deploying as config flag to edge now.

Leo: Also enabling prefix caching warmup for high-frequency keys to reduce first-hit load on the kv path.

oncall-sre: After 12m since mitigation: p95=360ms p99=620ms. I think immediate incident impact mitigated.

Ash: Next steps for postmortem: revert risky kv eviction change on canary, add contention tests to CI for heavy streaming workload, add instrumentation to kv lock latency, and add automated fallback to old path when lock latency > X ms.

Maya: I'll open a PR with the rollback and a small integration test that runs 500 concurrent streaming sessions.

Jordan: Support will compile impacted customer list and send follow-up with ETA and RCA when available.

oncall-sre: Closing on-call paging for this signal — moving to incident response (postmortem) channel. If any regression recurs, re-page.

Sam: Thanks everyone. Great triage. Action items: Maya(rollback + test), Ash(instrumentation + perf test), Leo(routing policy audit), Jordan(customer comms).

Maya: filing incident ticket now: INC-2039001, linking dashboards and logs.

deploy-bot: traffic-split rollback scheduled for 13:00 UTC if no recurrence.

oncall-sre: leaving a watch for 30m.

Maya: confirmed: canary rollback PR created -> https://git.internal/r/1234 (will roll to canary after tests if safe).

Jordan: sent customer update: "We have applied mitigations and are monitoring — expected full update with root cause and fix ETA by EOD."

oncall-sre: final metrics snapshot before handoff: p95=340ms p99=580ms, client aborts back to baseline. Handing off to SRE rotation for post-incident follow up.

Maya: marking follow-ups: add kv-lock SLI, increase canary validation window for streaming workloads, run chaos test that simulates eviction thrash.

Ash: will schedule perf run tomorrow morning.

Sam: Product note: customers affected were on mid-tier dedicated and hosted streaming. No billing or data loss reported.

oncall-sre: incident thread closed for live mitigation. Please continue follow-ups in #postmortems and link INC-2039001. :white_check_mark:
